title: Where I started
logline: Making videos with a friend, then a documentary channel of my own.

roles.title: Video Producer & Editor
roles.notes: Content writing, strategy, YouTube content, and end-to-end production.

roles.title: Co-Founder & Content Head
roles.aka: aka: I gave myself too many jobs
roles.notes: A documentary-focused social media platform. Worked on the content and overall direction. Built the visual identity, messaging, positioning and, most importantly, the content.

story:
I don't think I really started with a plan.
I started by making things.

I was working with Dhiru Monchik, a friend and a YouTuber with 4M+ subs today, writing scripts, designing thumbnails and stuff, editing his videos, shooting his videos and bla bla, basically all the things related to content.
I was learning mostly by doing.

And somewhere in between all of that, I started thinking...
What if I build something myself?

That became Dumb Project, a documentary channel with my school friend Vashu.
We wanted to make documentaries and build something of our own around it.
So suddenly I wasn't just thinking about videos anymore.

I was thinking about the name.
The identity.
The content.
How to package it.
How to get people to care about it.

Basically, I gave myself a lot of work for free.
But I loved it.
Because I was slowly discovering that I wasn't only interested in making things.

I liked figuring out what should be made in the first place.
And that changed something for me.
I started wondering what would happen if I got to do this with a much bigger playground.

I didn't know it then...
but something was already around the corner.

And then I joined...
notes: Basically, I gave myself a lot of work for free. But I loved it.
I liked figuring out what should be made in the first place.

title: The shift
logline: Proper teams, a much bigger audience, and learning why things work.

roles.title: Content Producer & Editor
roles.notes: Content strategy, YouTube content, and end-to-end production. Creative leadership on shoots, working with editors and designers, and getting things finished.

story:
I think this was the first time things started getting serious.
I joined Tech Burner thinking I knew a decent amount about content.
Turns out... I knew shit. 😭
Suddenly there were proper teams, workflows, deadlines, a much bigger audience and people actually waiting for the things we were making.

So I started experimenting again.
Different formats.
Different ways of telling things.
Different thumbnails.
Different edits.
Different ways of making people stop scrolling.

And because there was so much happening, I slowly started getting curious about everything around the content too.
Why did this work?
Why did that flop?
Why does changing one tiny thing suddenly make something perform?
I started moving from just making the thing to actually thinking about why we were making it.

I also got to build and work with a team of designers, editors, writers and creators.
That taught me something I didn't really understand before:
making something yourself is easy, but getting 10 people to make it together is the actual problem.

Tech Burner was probably where I realised that I could do more than just design or edit.
I could actually figure things out.
And once I realised that...
I wanted to see what else I could do.

Turns out, I was about to find out.
Because just when things started making sense, the whole team decided to move to Bangalore.
And I wasn't going with them. (just single child problems)
(to be continued)
notes: Making something yourself is easy. Getting 10 people to make it together is the actual problem.

title: Bigger problem
logline: Seeing the business behind the creator.

roles.title: Creative Producer
roles.notes: Brand campaigns and content ideation, planning and execution for clients. Leading teams of designers and editors, and turning a client brief into something worth watching.

story:
So... I quit Tech Burner.
The team was moving to Bangalore, and for me, that just wasn't possible.
I'm a single child from Haridwar, and my parents were not really comfortable sending me that far away.

So there wasn't much to think about.
I had to start looking again.

For almost two months, I was just trying to find the next thing.
Applying.
Talking to people.
Looking at companies.
Wondering if I should continue doing what I was doing or try something completely different.

Eventually, I landed at Monk Entertainment.
And this time, I walked into a slightly different world.
Till then, I had mostly been on the creator side.

At Monk, I started seeing what happens behind the creator.
Brands.
Clients.
Campaigns.
Pitches.
Budgets.
Deadlines.

I started understanding that content isn't just about making something cool.
There is a business behind it.
A reason why the brand is spending money.
A reason why the audience should care.
And a reason why the idea needs to work.

I started looking at my work differently.
Not just: “Does this look good?”
But also: “Does this make sense?”
That was new for me.

I came here thinking I was going to learn more about content.
I ended up learning a lot more about the business of content.
And once I started seeing that side...
I wanted to go even deeper.

Things were going pretty well at Monk.
I was working from home, getting to understand the business side of content and seeing what happens behind the creator.
Then, after a few months, they asked me to join them at the Mumbai office.

And I thought...
Bangalore nahi jaa paya, Mumbai kaise jaaunga bhai. 😂

So yeah, once again, I had to start looking.
But this time, I had a slightly different thought.
I had already seen one side of the industry.
Then I got to see what happens behind it.
Maybe it was time to see what happens on the other side.
I just didn't know it yet. hehe
notes: Bangalore nahi jaa paya, Mumbai kaise jaaunga bhai. 😂
Not just “does this look good?” but also “does this make sense?”

title: Bigger picture
logline: Building for one brand, and figuring out this whole AI thing.

roles.title: Content & Growth Lead
roles.notes: I ideated, planned and created content for social media, performance, educational channels, the app and digital channels. I used AI tools and workflows to support content ideation and creative production, and handled content from idea to production and publishing.

story:
So after Monk, I started looking again.
And this time I was thinking a little differently.

Till now, I had mostly lived inside the content world.
First making content with my friend.
Then working in a content-driven org.
Then understanding the business behind all of it.

Now I was curious about what happens when you're actually trying to build something for a brand.
And that's how I ended up at CashKaro.

It felt different from everything I had done before.
There was no creator waiting for the next video.
No client asking for a content calendar.

Now there was a brand to think about and just one direction.
What should we say?
How should we say it?
Where should it live?
And most importantly...
why should anyone care?

I started getting involved in campaigns, content, performance, activation and retention marketing, and all the random things that sit somewhere between marketing and making stuff.
And I really liked that.

Because I could finally use all the things I had picked up along the way.
The edit and design brain from the beginning.
The content brain from Tech Burner.
The business understanding from Monk.
And then, somewhere along the way, I started figuring out this whole AI thing.

At first, I was just playing with it.
Making weird stuff. Trying different tools. Breaking things. Trying again.

But slowly I started seeing where it could actually be useful for brands.
Not just “look, AI can make this.”
More like:
“Can this help us make something faster?”
“Can we try an idea that would normally take too much time?”
“Can we use it to make the brand do something it couldn't do before?”
That's when it got interesting for me.

I started looking at AI less like a cool new tool and more like another part of the creative process.
Except now all these things had to work together.

And that was probably the first time I felt like:
Oh shit. Maybe all those different things I was doing were actually adding up.

Maybe I wasn't jumping from one thing to another.
Maybe I was just collecting things.
notes: …and most importantly, why should anyone care?
Maybe I was just collecting things.

title: Putting it all together
logline: AI-led creative for brands that have to perform.

roles.title: Brand & Creative Strategist
roles.notes: I work on AI-led creative workflows and brand content that has to perform, not just look good. My work covers creative strategy, content production, and building systems that let good creative get made repeatedly.

story:
By this point, I had collected quite a few things.
The edit and design brain from the beginning.
The content brain from Tech Burner.
The business understanding from Monk.
The brand thinking from CashKaro.

And somewhere along the way, I had started getting really curious about AI.
Not because I wanted to become an “AI guy”.
I just had a lot of ideas.
And sometimes the problem was that I couldn't make them fast enough.

So I started using AI to close that gap.
I'd have some vague idea in my head...
“What if we tried this?”
And instead of spending days figuring out whether it was even possible, I could just try it.

Make something.
Break it.
Change it.
Try another version.

Sometimes the idea was shit.
Sometimes the AI was shit.
Sometimes both of us were shit. 😂

But sometimes...
it worked.
And that’s when it became interesting.

I started figuring out how these tools could actually fit into the way brands work.
Not replacing the thinking.
Not replacing the craft.
Just making the distance between “I have an idea” and “let's see it” much shorter.

And that changed the way I started working.
I could explore more.
Test more.
Make more versions.
Take an idea that was sitting somewhere in my head and actually build it.
So now all those things I had picked up over the years had to work together.

And honestly...
I'll say it again.
Maybe all those random things I was doing were actually adding up.
Maybe I wasn't jumping from one thing to another.
Maybe I was just collecting things.
And now I'm finally figuring out what I can do with all of them.
notes: Sometimes both of us were shit. 😂
The distance between “I have an idea” and “let’s see it”, much shorter.
